evidence: The project is a Django app (fcm-django) with clear separation into logical modules: models, api, admin, fields, settings, migrations, tests, etc.
APIs are implemented as separate modules (rest_framework.py, tastypie.py) but co-located within the same package, indicating bounded contexts rather than decoupled services.
All components (models, API endpoints, admin, tests) are part of a single deployable Python package (fcm_django), with no indication of inter-process or network communication.
Use of Django’s internal mechanisms (ORM, migrations, admin, signals) tightly binds data and behavior within one runtime.
No external service dependencies beyond Firebase Admin SDK (used synchronously in code), confirming no microservice-style async/remote dependencies.
Strong cohesion within modules (e.g., fcm_django/api/ contains all API logic) and low coupling via well-defined interfaces (e.g., swapper for model abstraction).
risks: Tight integration with Django internals may reduce portability or increase refactoring effort for future decoupling.
Monolithic deployment scope limits scalability and team autonomy compared to true microservices.
Possible coupling through shared models (Device) and global settings (FCM_DJANGO_SETTINGS) could hinder modularity over time if not carefully managed.
